jobs.description:
About Citco

JOB DESCRIPTION

The market leader. The premier provider. The best in the business. At Citco, we’ve been the front-runner in our field since our incorporation in 1948 led to the evolution of the asset servicing sector itself. This pioneering spirit continues to guide us today as we innovate and expand, push beyond the boundaries of our industry, and shape its future. From working exclusively with hedge funds to serving all alternatives, corporations and private clients, our organization has grown immensely across asset classes and geographies. For us, this progress is a pattern that we’ll only maintain as we move forward, always prioritizing our performance. So for those who want to play at the top of their game and be at the vanguard of their space, we say: Welcome to Citco.

About The Team & Business Line

Fund Administration is Citco’s core business, and our alternative asset and accounting service is one of the industry’s most respected. Our continuous investment in learning and technology solutions means our people are equipped to deliver a seamless client experience.

A challenging and exciting role in a rapidly growing industry, Portfolio Analytics services across a diverse client base spanning hedge funds, private markets and multi-asset strategies across North America, the United Kingdom, Continental Europe and Asia. The Vice President of the Portfolio Analytics group will take a senior leadership role managing existing US client relationships, ensuring client retention, and driving sales, marketing and business development initiatives across the region. The team provides ad-hoc and regulatory risk reports that include, but are not limited to, exposure and P&L reports, limits monitoring, scenario analysis, stress testing, value-at-risk and fund performance analytics - supporting clients across a broad range of strategies and structures.

The role provides a unique opportunity to work closely with a wide range of securities, derivatives and structured products in many currencies traded across global markets, and to lead the build-out of a structured, high-performing client service model across the US book. The individual's duties will include, but are not limited to, client onboarding project management, senior client relationship leadership, team management, and the training and development of staff — mirroring and helping to embed a proven operating model already established elsewhere in the group.

Responsibilities

Your Role:

Business Development & Commercial Acumen — Take an active, leading role in the CFS 'new business acquisition' process from a Portfolio Analytics perspective, effectively demonstrating our suite of Portfolio Analytics services to potential clients as well as new or enhanced services to existing clients, positioning this as a core driver of the role; evaluate the viability of current and new business proposals with emphasis on tactical issues and barriers
Client Relationship Management — Own and lead senior client relationships across the US book, participating in regular client calls and working closely with the global Client Integration team who oversee and project manage the firm-wide onboarding process
Reporting of Client KPIs — Own and maintain the KPI and RAG framework across the US client base, supervising junior team members in day-to-day tracking and reporting to support senior management oversight
Team Leadership & Management — Provide day-to-day leadership and management of the US Portfolio Analytics team, embedding a structured, KPI-driven client service model and ensuring consistent standards of client oversight and RAG reporting across the book
Communication — Use appropriate interpersonal styles and techniques to gain acceptance and help others understand the importance of the vision on the day-to-day reality of the risk reporting process
Building Networks - Proactively build strong relationships with Client Service and Business Development colleagues across CFS offices as a first priority, while also networking across departments (Valuation/Profit & Loss, Operations, Internal Audit, Integration, etc.) to establish collaborative business relationships at all levels and facilitate the accomplishment of business objectives
Leading & Managing Others — Embody the CFS culture, lead and inspire team through change, encourage others to seek opportunities for different approaches to address problems and opportunities
Organization & Resource Management — Oversee the US team with responsibility for pre-sales, onboarding, client coverage planning, and other new business initiatives
Building and Retaining Organizational Talent —Focus on identifying, developing, deploying and retaining key talent within the US team (including succession planning) for the future success of CFS, initiating strategies to develop internal talent through ongoing training and conducting timely performance evaluations.
Operational Decision-making — Commit and take responsibility for tactical decisions, adopting innovative approaches to move resolution of challenges to completion; communicate outcomes to all stakeholders and contribute to CFS vision and strategy
Execution — Execute business strategy by aligning communication, accountabilities, skills, internal processes and measurement to ensure sustainable and profitable results
Client Risk & Continuity Oversight — Identify and manage clients with elevated customisation and key person risk, ensuring documented continuity plans are in place and escalating concentration risk where appropriate

Qualifications

About You:

Drive for Results — Possessing an energetic and tenacious achievement orientation; proactively seeking opportunities to drive performance of self and team, and setting stretching goals; managing personal and group strengths and opportunities
Navigating Complexity — Proactively and quickly making sense of complex issues where ambiguity exists; communicating complicated information concisely and logically
Excellent analytical, problem-solving and communication skills, with proven ability to summarise and interpret client requirements
Aspiration to become a subject matter expert in proprietary risk solutions
Someone who enjoys project-based work, collaboration across teams, and dealing directly with clients — no two days the same
Quantitative background with a Bachelor's/higher level degree or professional qualification (MSc, PhD, CQF, FRM, PRMIA, GARP, CFA, FIA)
Proficient in Excel, VBA, SQL, with Python experience in particular advantageous
Knowledge of business intelligence tools such as Qlik Sense (or Tableau) and Jaspersoft is a plus
7–10 years' experience in investment and regulatory risk reporting and performance analytics in funds/asset management/banking/insurance - including hedge fund, private markets and multi-asset strategies , with demonstrated experience in client relationship leadership, team management, pre-sales, onboarding and business development
Prior experience managing or supervising a client-facing team is required
Knowledge of market, credit, liquidity and counterparty risk measurement and management under regulatory frameworks such as Form PF, Form CPO-PQR, Annex IV, Basel III/CRD IV/CRR and Solvency II is advantageous
Candidates must be willing to travel to the United States for business purposes

Salary Range:
$115,000 - 155,000

Our Benefits

Your well-being is of paramount importance and central to our success here at Citco. Citco offers a comprehensive and competitive total rewards package to support your career success and personal needs. Your base salary will be determined by several factors such as the role, experience, skillset, market conditions, etc. Furthermore, qualifying positions can participate in an annual discretionary bonus pool based on company profitability and individual contributions. Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, short and long-term disability benefits, a retirement savings plan, tuition reimbursement, mental health and wellness support, parental leave, and more. We believe that an inclusive workforce not only enriches our company but also drives us towards greater success.

jobs.title: Head of Artificial Intelligence
jobs.description:
Enterprise AI | Manufacturing | Supply Chain | Private Label | Business Transformation

Scope:
Enterprise-wide, multi-site
Locations:
Toronto, Wixom, Chicago and Sardis; regular site travel required
Role model:
High-leverage individual contributor / transformation owner, supported by internal teams, vendors and consultants
Primary measure:
Measurable business value from AI-enabled process and decision improvement

About the Company

The company is a large contract manufacturer and packager of household cleaning products serving branded and private-label customers across North America.

Position Overview

This position will define and drive the company’s practical adoption of artificial intelligence across the business. This is not primarily an IT infrastructure, software development or research role. It is a business transformation role for someone who can understand how the company makes money, how its plants and customer programs operate, where decisions and processes break down, and where AI can create measurable advantage.
The person will own the AI opportunity portfolio from discovery through value realization: identifying and sizing high-value use cases, redesigning workflows and decision processes, determining data and technology requirements, coordinating internal and external technical resources, guiding pilots into scaled deployment, building organizational capability, and measuring financial and operational results.
The role will initially operate as a high-leverage individual contributor. Success depends less on personally building every model and more on asking the right questions, selecting the right problems, challenging vendors and specialists, and ensuring solutions are adopted in the business and sustained.

Core Mandate

Build a phased enterprise AI roadmap tied directly to company business priorities, plant economics and customer-program economics.
Create a repeatable method for finding, evaluating and prioritizing AI opportunities based on value, feasibility, data readiness, adoption requirements and risk.
Turn selected opportunities into implemented solutions that change how work is performed and how decisions are made, rather than producing disconnected pilots or demonstrations.
Develop the internal operating model, governance, external partner ecosystem and AI literacy required to scale successful solutions across facilities and functions.
Own value realization: each meaningful initiative should have a baseline, business case, accountable owner, adoption plan and measurable outcome.

Key Responsibilities

1. AI Strategy, Opportunity Portfolio & Roadmap
Develop and maintain the enterprise AI transformation roadmap across manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, quality, R&D/formulation, commercialization, commercial/customer processes, finance and supporting functions.
Build a decision and process inventory to identify repetitive, high-value, data-rich business situations where AI, automation or advanced analytics can materially improve outcomes.
Prioritize use cases by expected economic value, strategic importance, feasibility, data readiness, scalability, change impact and risk; stop low-value or poorly grounded initiatives early.
Continuously assess the AI landscape—including generative AI, agents, machine learning, computer vision, optimization, digital twins and industrial AI—and translate relevant advances into practical recommendations for the company.

2. Manufacturing & Intelligent Operations
Work directly with plant, engineering, maintenance, quality and operations leaders to identify AI-enabled improvements in process control, batch optimization, yield, quality, line performance, changeovers, reliability, downtime, energy, waste and safety.
Identify opportunities for predictive quality, predictive maintenance, machine vision, intelligent scheduling, digital twins and decision support where the operational data and economics justify them.
Design pilots with clear operating baselines and success measures, then create the playbook required to replicate proven solutions across relevant sites and assets.
Ensure AI is embedded into standard operating processes and decision routines with appropriate human oversight, rather than operating as a separate technology layer.

3. Contract Manufacturing, Customer Programs & Commercialization
Apply AI to the full customer-program lifecycle, including opportunity identification, RFQ/quoting, formulation and product development, packaging/specification management, commercialization, production readiness, fulfillment and ongoing program profitability.
Develop better decision support around bid/no-bid, pricing floors, capacity implications, changeover burden, working capital, forecast reliability, customer service requirements and true program economics.
Explore AI-enabled customer and category intelligence that can identify assortment gaps, private-label opportunities, cross-sell opportunities, packaging gaps and product concepts the company can proactively bring to customers.
Use connected data to improve launch execution, specification/artwork consistency, retailer/customer compliance, deductions/chargebacks and root-cause learning from complaints and service failures.

4. Supply Chain, Procurement & Planning
Identify AI opportunities in forecasting, S&OP/IBP, inventory, raw-material planning, procurement, sourcing, supplier intelligence, production scheduling, warehousing and transportation.
Improve the company’s ability to predict customer demand and forecast reliability, allocate capacity and materials, sequence production and manage working capital under uncertainty.
Use AI to surface exceptions and recommended actions so teams can spend less time assembling information and more time resolving the decisions that matter.

5. Data, Technology & Partner Orchestration
Define practical data-readiness requirements for AI use cases and work with IT, plant systems, Finance, Quality, R&D and other data owners to improve access, context and reliability.
Evaluate AI platforms, specialist vendors, consultants and implementation partners based on business fit, architecture, security, scalability, interoperability, total cost and expected value.
Make informed build-vs-buy-vs-partner recommendations and ensure the company retains appropriate knowledge, control and portability as capabilities scale.
Act as the business product owner for AI initiatives while technical specialists own the detailed engineering, infrastructure and model construction where appropriate.

6. Governance, Risk & Responsible AI
Establish proportionate AI governance covering privacy, cybersecurity, customer confidentiality and IP, data access, model risk, human oversight, transparency, validation and regulatory requirements.
Create clear decision rights defining where AI may inform, recommend or execute, and where human approval remains required.
Ensure use cases involving regulated products, quality systems or customer-sensitive information are developed and validated with the appropriate functional experts.

7. Change, Adoption & Capability Building
Build AI literacy among executives, plant leaders, managers and frontline users through practical education tied to the company’s work rather than generic technology training.
Create a network of functional and site champions who can identify opportunities, support adoption and help scale what works.
Address resistance, role changes, trust and skill gaps directly; redesign processes and responsibilities where AI changes how work should be performed.
Communicate wins, failures and lessons openly so the organization becomes progressively better at selecting and deploying AI.

8. Value Realization & Executive Reporting
Build business cases and establish measurable baselines before meaningful investment is made.
Track value across cost, margin, working capital, throughput, yield, quality, service, innovation speed, risk reduction and employee productivity as relevant to each use case.
Maintain a portfolio view of AI investments, adoption and realized value, and report progress, risks and priorities to senior leadership.
Treat adoption and sustained operating impact—not the number of pilots launched—as the primary definition of success.

Illustrative Initial Opportunity Areas

Manufacturing:
Batch/process optimization; predictive quality; machine vision; maintenance/reliability; line scheduling/changeovers; energy, yield and waste.
Product & R&D:
Formulation optimization; raw-material substitution; experiment prioritization; specification knowledge; faster customer/product development.
Supply Chain:
Demand forecasting; customer forecast quality; inventory; procurement; supplier intelligence; production planning; logistics and working capital.
Private Label / Commercial:
RFQ and quote intelligence; bid/no-bid; customer/program profitability; assortment whitespace; cross-sell; customer opportunity intelligence.
Commercialization & Quality:
Launch control tower; specification/artwork consistency; complaints-to-root-cause; regulatory/product-stewardship impact analysis; customer compliance.
Knowledge & Administration:
Plant/SOP/maintenance knowledge assistants; document processing; management reporting; finance and back-office workflow automation.

Candidate Profile

The strongest candidate is likely an experienced manufacturing, operations, supply-chain, analytics or business-transformation leader who has become sophisticated in AI—not necessarily a career AI researcher or software engineer. Because modern generative AI and agent technologies are new, depth of practical use and demonstrated outcomes matter more than an arbitrary number of years with “AI” in a title.
Typically 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, operations, supply chain, digital/business transformation, advanced analytics or a closely related environment.
Demonstrated recent ownership of meaningful AI, advanced-analytics, automation or digital-transformation initiatives from problem definition through deployment and measurable business impact.
Strong understanding of manufacturing economics and operational processes; experience in process manufacturing, CPG, chemicals, private label, contract manufacturing or other complex multi-site industrial environments is strongly preferred.
Practical fluency in current AI capabilities, including generative AI, AI agents, machine learning, predictive analytics, optimization, computer vision and intelligent automation. The candidate does not need to personally code every solution, but must understand enough to challenge technical assumptions and vendors.
Strong financial and business acumen: can build a credible business case, quantify value, understand trade-offs and distinguish an interesting technology from an investable business opportunity.
Proven ability to lead through influence across plant operations, engineering, supply chain, quality, R&D, Finance, IT/data teams and senior leadership without necessarily owning those functions directly.
Experience working with external consultants, software/platform providers and specialist technical partners; capable of making build/buy/partner decisions.
Excellent facilitation and communication skills, from plant-floor working sessions to executive presentations.
Comfort with ambiguity and an entrepreneurial bias toward practical experimentation, learning and scale.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, Computer/Data Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degree is beneficial but not required.
Ability and willingness to travel regularly among company facilities as projects require.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 Days
Visit key company sites and build a grounded view of operations, customer-program workflows, current systems/data and organizational readiness.
Create an enterprise AI opportunity map and prioritized initial roadmap with business cases, data requirements,

jobs.title: Interim Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Chief Information Officer

Reports to: President

Location: Greater Toronto Area, Ontario

Duration: 6-12 Months

Hybrid working

Our client, a large and complex Ontario post-secondary institution, is seeking an accomplished Interim Chief Information Officer
to provide leadership through an important period of transition, modernization and organizational evolution.

This is an exciting opportunity for a seasoned technology executive who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution
.

The organization recognizes that technology has the potential to play a much greater role in how it operates, how decisions are made, how services are delivered and how students experience the institution. The Interim CIO will be asked not simply to manage the existing technology environment, but to challenge conventional thinking about how technology is deployed and where it can fundamentally improve the operating model.

Leading a team of more than 100 technology professionals, the successful executive will initially provide stability, clarity and leadership through transition. Beyond this, they will help establish the priorities, capabilities, operating model and roadmap required for the next stage of the organization's technology journey.

This is therefore a mandate for a builder, modernizer and objective disruptor
, someone able to respect what is working while constructively challenging what could be done differently.

The Mandate

The Interim CIO will provide overall leadership to the technology function while working closely with the organization's senior leadership team to determine how technology can better enable its academic, student and operational priorities.

A central component of the mandate will be assessing the technology operating model
and identifying opportunities to improve effectiveness, service, scalability and value.
The Interim CIO will be expected to create alignment between technology strategy and organizational strategy, while maintaining a bias toward execution and measurable outcomes.

Key priorities will include:

Technology Strategy & Operating Model

Assess the current technology environment, capabilities, organizational structure and priorities and establish a clear roadmap for the next phase of modernization.
Challenge existing assumptions around how technology services are organized, delivered and supported.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce complexity, improve scalability and improve the value generated from technology investment
.
Evaluate the appropriate balance between internal capabilities, external partnerships, managed services and selective outsourcing.
Introduce stronger prioritization and governance disciplines to ensure technology resources are focused on the areas of greatest institutional impact.
Translate technology strategy into a practical execution agenda with clear accountabilities and outcomes.

Leadership Through Change

The Interim CIO will inherit a substantial team of 100+ technology professionals
and will need to quickly establish credibility and provide visible, confident leadership.

The organization operates within a unionized environment. Accordingly, the executive must understand how to lead meaningful organizational and operational change while respecting collective agreements, established processes and employee relationships.

The successful individual will:

Provide stability and clarity during transition.
Assess organizational capability, structure and accountabilities.
Coach and develop technology leaders.
Build stronger accountability for results.
Engage employees in the modernization journey.
Create a strong service and performance culture.
Navigate change thoughtfully within a complex unionized environment
.
Maintain momentum while making difficult decisions where required.

ERP Optimization & Enterprise Platforms

An important priority will be continuing to optimize the organization's ERP and broader enterprise technology environment.

The Interim CIO will:

Assess the current ERP implementation and identify opportunities to increase adoption, functionality and organizational value.
Address process, integration, data and operating-model issues that may inhibit the organization from realizing the full value of its enterprise platforms.
Challenge the proliferation of unnecessary processes, applications and workarounds where these create complexity.
Ensure technology modernization is accompanied by process modernization rather than simply automating existing ways of working
.
Strengthen the connection between enterprise systems, organizational processes and user experience.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Resilience

Cybersecurity will be a significant part of the mandate.

The Interim CIO will assess and evolve the organization's cybersecurity posture, governance and protocols, ensuring they remain appropriate for a large, complex and highly distributed post-secondary environment.

The executive will work to strengthen areas including security governance, accountability, organizational awareness and operational resilience, while ensuring cybersecurity is understood as an enterprise risk rather than simply an IT responsibility
.

The successful candidate will balance increasingly sophisticated security requirements with the accessibility, flexibility and innovation expected within a modern educational institution.

Cloud & Technology Modernization

The organization has begun elements of its cloud journey, but further opportunity remains to modernize its technology architecture and operating environment.

The Interim CIO will assess where further migration and modernization create genuine operational, financial, resilience or user-experience benefits.

They will bring an objective perspective regarding cloud strategy, legacy environments, technical debt, architecture and application rationalization
, ensuring modernization is driven by institutional value rather than technology for technology's sake.

Data Governance, Analytics & Decision Support

Data represents a significant opportunity for the organization.

The Interim CIO will help establish stronger data governance, ownership, quality and analytics capabilities
, enabling leaders across the institution to make better and faster decisions based on reliable information.

The mandate will include helping the organization move beyond reporting toward a culture where trusted data and actionable insights routinely inform operational, financial, academic and student-focused decision-making.

This will require both technology leadership and the ability to address the governance, accountability and behavioural changes necessary to establish a more mature data culture.

Artificial Intelligence

The organization recognizes the potentially significant role AI could play in both its operating model and the broader evolution of post-secondary education.

The Interim CIO will help leadership distinguish between experimentation and sustainable enterprise adoption, identifying practical opportunities where AI, automation and emerging technologies can improve productivity, decision-making and service delivery
.

Equally important will be establishing appropriate governance around the adoption of these technologies, including cybersecurity, privacy, data, risk and responsible use.

The successful executive will bring curiosity and ambition around AI while maintaining the pragmatic judgment required to translate emerging technology into sustainable institutional value.

The Evolving Student Experience

Technology is increasingly integral to the complete student journey.

How students learn, interact with faculty, access services, consume information and engage with an institution continues to evolve.

The Interim CIO will work across the organization to consider how technology can help create a simpler, more integrated, personalized and contemporary student experience
.

The opportunity extends beyond classroom technology. It is about understanding how technology can differentiate the institution and reduce friction across the entire student journey.

Service Culture

A key leadership priority will be continuing to evolve the technology function toward a highly responsive, accountable and customer-focused service organization.

The Interim CIO will establish clear expectations around service delivery, ownership, responsiveness and partnership with internal stakeholders.

Technology should increasingly be viewed as an enabler and partner to the organization
, rather than simply a provider of systems and infrastructure.

The Ideal Interim Executive

The successful candidate will be an accomplished CIO or senior enterprise technology executive
who has led a sizeable, complex technology function through significant modernization and organizational change.

They will bring experience across a combination of:

Enterprise technology strategy and execution.
Leadership of large, multidisciplinary technology teams.
Technology operating-model transformation.
ERP and enterprise application optimization.
Cloud migration and modernization.
Cybersecurity, risk and technology governance.
Data governance, analytics and information management.
AI, automation and emerging technologies.
Process optimization and organizational simplification.
Managed services, strategic sourcing and outsourcing.
Vendor and commercial management.
Digital/customer experience transformation.
Leadership in a unionized environment.
Organizational change and talent development.

Experience within higher education or the broader public sector
would be highly relevant, although the organization will also be interested in executives from other large, complex and regulated environments who can bring fresh thinking and transferable experience.

Leadership Style

This mandate requires more than technical credibility.

The ideal executive will be pragmatic, curious, commercially minded and comfortable challenging the status quo
. They will know when to listen and preserve institutional knowledge, but equally when to push the organization toward a different approach.

They will be capable of moving comfortably between the boardroom and the technology organization, translating complex technology issues into clear discussions about risk, cost, service, productivity and organizational outcomes
.

Most importantly, this individual will be an objective disruptor with strong execution discipline
.
They will leave the organization not simply with better technology, but with a stronger technology function, clearer priorities, improved governance, better use of data, enhanced cybersecurity and a pragmatic roadmap for how technology can enable the institution's future operating model.

The attraction of the assignment

For an experienced CIO, this is a rare opportunity to have meaningful impact in a relatively short period.

The mandate combines people leadership, technology modernization, ERP optimization, cyber, cloud, data and analytics, AI, operating-model transformation and student experience
within one of the most rapidly changing sectors in Canada.

The successful interim will have the platform to challenge existing thinking, accelerate decisions and help redefine the role technology plays across the institution.

This is not a mandate to simply keep the lights on. It is an opportunity to shape what technology leadership, capability and service should look like for the organization's next chapter.

jobs.description:
Permanent Full Time

Director, Technical Solutions

Our Digital Strategy and Design team is looking for a Director, Technical Solutions
to lead the delivery of high-quality digital solutions in partnership with business and technology teams.

This hands-on technology leader will guide solutions from design through production, set engineering direction and work with architecture, cybersecurity and enterprise platform teams to deliver secure, reliable outcomes.

What you will do:

In this role, you will co-lead a cross-functional team with the Product Owner, translating product outcomes into an executable technical plan and remaining close enough to the work to guide design, code, integration, testing, release and production support.

You will establish reusable engineering foundations, automated quality and security controls, and operational practices that increase delivery speed, improve reliability and reduce duplication across teams. Key accountabilities will also include the following:

Own end-to-end technical delivery across experience, application, API, integration, data and cloud layers, making pragmatic design decisions within enterprise architecture guardrails
Remain hands-on through architecture spikes, code and design reviews, troubleshooting automation and critical-path delivery while enabling engineers to own implementation
Apply AI-based technologies where they create measurable value, including generative AI, intelligent automation and AI-assisted software delivery, with appropriate data, privacy, security, model-risk and human-oversight controls
Establish full-stack engineering standards for user experience, accessability, performance, API design, data handling, observability, testing and maintainability

What you will bring:

Degree/diploma in computer science or related discipline, or equivalent combination of training and experience
A minimum of 10+ years’ related experience delivering digital products and technology platforms, including accountability for solution design, engineering execution, release and production health
Deep technologist with recent hands-on software delivery experience in roles such as Engineering Lead, Technical Lead or Solutions Architect
Demonstrated full-stack expertise across modern web or mobile experiences, backend services, APIs, integrations, data stores and cloud infrastructure
Strong understanding of distributed-system design, including event-driven architecture, microservices, consistency, scalability, resiliency, observability and failure recovery
Experience applying AI-based technologies—including generative AI or machine learning capabilities—to production use cases, with knowledge of responsible AI, privacy, security, data quality, evaluation and monitoring
Demonstrated ability to make and communicate technical trade-offs across scope, time, cost, risk, quality and long-term maintainability
Experience working in a complex, regulated and rapidly evolving environment with high expectations for security, reliability and execution
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical decisions, options and risks to technical and non-technical audiences

Assets:

Experience in financial services, preferably insurance
Experience modernizing applications, decomposing and rationalizing systems, and integrating with core or legacy platforms
Experience delivering omnichannel experiences using cloud-native architecture
Knowledge of business and continuous architecture practices, architecture modelling tools and frameworks such as UML, ArchiMate and TOGAF; TOGAF certification is an asset

The base salary for this position is between $149,000 - $199,000
annually. This represents base salary only and does not represent other variable compensation components of our total compensation ( i.e. annual bonus, commission etc). jobs.title: Chief Technology and Information Officer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description

POSITION PURPOSE SUMMARY

The Chief Technology and Information Officer (CTIO) provides enterprise leadership and strategic direction for technology, information systems, data, cybersecurity and digital capabilities across The Salvation Army Canada and Bermuda Territory.

As a senior organizational leader, the CTIO ensures technology strategy and investment support The Salvation Army’s mission, strategic priorities and operational needs. The role is accountable for technology, cybersecurity and resilience, enterprise systems, data and digital capability, technology operations, vendor partnerships, financial stewardship and the ongoing development of a high-performing technology function.

Working across a large, geographically dispersed and decentralized organization, the CTIO builds trusted relationships with leaders and stakeholders, balances enterprise consistency with operational realities, and drives technology adoption and organizational efficiencies in a way that reflects The Salvation Army’s mission, values and culture.

Accountabilities

Mission, Culture and Organizational Leadership

Authentically lead in alignment with The Salvation Army’s mission, vision, values, Christian identity and spiritual foundations, recognizing that its social and community services are expressions of its higher purpose to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in communities.
Ensure technology strategy, investment and decision-making ultimately enable people, ministry and services to advance the mission.
Contribute as an enterprise leader to organizational strategy, priorities and decisions beyond the technology portfolio.
Balance enterprise standards and priorities with legitimate operational, geographic and ministry-specific needs.

Executive and People Leadership

Build and lead a high-performing technology leadership team with clear accountability, a service-oriented culture, strong succession and workforce planning, and the appropriate balance of internal and external capability.
Provide strategic advice to senior leadership, translating complex technology, cybersecurity, data and digital issues into clear organizational choices, risks, opportunities and investment decisions.
Lead significant organizational change associated with technology transformation, recognizing that successful adoption depends on people, process, culture and technology.
Build strong relationships with operational leaders and users to understand needs and continuously improve technology effectiveness.
Model strong stewardship, integrity and accountability in leadership and decision-making.

Enterprise Technology Strategy

Develop and execute a multi-year enterprise technology strategy aligned with organizational priorities and mission.
Stabilize and simplify the technology environment, strengthening reliability, integration, interoperability and sustainable adoption.
Optimize existing technology platforms and investments before introducing new solutions.
Improve connectivity and interoperability between systems to create a more seamless technology and user environment.
Establish technology roadmaps, portfolio governance and prioritization that sequence investments appropriately and balance innovation, affordability, risk, organizational readiness and capacity.
Lead targeted modernization and transformation where it creates clear organizational value, while assessing emerging technologies thoughtfully.
Oversee the technology project and investment portfolio, ensuring appropriate governance, stakeholder engagement and benefits realization.

Cybersecurity, Data and Technology Risk

Provide executive oversight of cybersecurity, information security, privacy, technology risk and resilience.
Ensure appropriate controls, governance and compliance are in place to protect organizational information, systems and technology assets.
Maintain effective disaster recovery, business continuity and technology resilience capabilities.
Ensure security, privacy, data protection and risk considerations are embedded in technology investments, vendor relationships and emerging technology adoption.

Technology Operations and Service Delivery

Ensure reliable, secure, responsive and cost-effective delivery of enterprise applications, infrastructure, networks, cloud services, end-user technology and service management.
Establish service standards, performance measures and continuous improvement practices that strengthen user experience and technology effectiveness.
Maintain an enterprise technology architecture that supports integration, scalability, security and future organizational requirements.

Financial, Vendor and Investment Stewardship – Money, Sourcing and Commercial Discipline

Lead technology operating and capital budgets and multi-year investment planning, ensuring investments demonstrate strategic value, affordability and sustainability.
Oversee business cases, cost-benefit analysis and benefits realization for significant technology investments.
Establish effective sourcing strategies and lead strategic vendor relationships, contract performance and commercial negotiations.
Drive cost effectiveness through technology simplification, optimization, disciplined sourcing and effective management of technology assets and services.

Strategic Business Enablement, Data and Artificial Intelligence

Connect technology, data and digital priorities directly to organizational strategy, mission outcomes, service delivery and measurable value.
Act as an enterprise integrator across ministries, functions and geographies, using technology and data to simplify processes, strengthen service delivery and improve decision-making.
Lead enterprise data strategy, governance, stewardship, quality, analytics and reporting to enable trusted and actionable information.
Establish and oversee responsible AI and automation governance, ensuring use cases are mission-aligned, secure, ethical, legally compliant, operationally practical and supported by appropriate human oversight.
Establish governance and performance measures that allow senior leaders to monitor technology value, data maturity, digital adoption and AI readiness.

Education, Experience And Qualifications

Mission and Organizational Alignment

Demonstrated alignment with and ability to authentically lead within The Salvation Army’s mission, values and Christian foundations.
Demonstrated understanding that The Salvation Army’s social and community services are expressions of a broader mission to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in communities.
Ability to operate effectively within a large, complex, values-based and decentralized organization.
Demonstrated commitment to ethical leadership, stewardship, collaboration and service.

Education And Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Engineering or a related discipline is required.
Master’s degree in Business Administration, Technology, Information Systems or a related field may be considered an asset.
Relevant executive technology, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, governance or program management certifications may be an asset.
An equivalent combination of education and significant relevant executive experience may be considered.

Experience and Knowledge

Significant progressive leadership experience in technology, information systems, digital or related discipline, including substantial senior executive or enterprise leadership experience.
Demonstrated success developing and executing enterprise technology strategies and leading transformation or modernization.
Experience leading technology within a large, complex, multi-site and/or geographically dispersed organization.
Broad executive-level understanding of enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, data, integration, digital capability and technology operations.
Demonstrated experience overseeing cybersecurity, technology risk, resilience and business continuity.
Experience with enterprise data governance, analytics and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.
Significant experience managing technology budgets, investment decisions, strategic vendors and major contracts.
Proven success in building and developing high-performing leadership teams.
Demonstrated experience leading complex organizational change and influencing senior stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience advising executive leadership and governance bodies on technology strategy, investment, cybersecurity, risk and organizational implications.
Experience in a decentralized, faith-based, not-for-profit, healthcare, public sector or similarly complex service organization is considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience establishing or maturing enterprise data strategies, data governance, analytics capability and information management practices across a complex organization.
Experience reviewing, governing and deploying artificial intelligence or advanced automation capabilities with appropriate attention to ethics, privacy, cybersecurity, risk, adoption, benefits realization and operational readiness.

Skills And Leadership Capabilities

Strategic enterprise thinker who connects technology, data and digital priorities to organizational strategy and mission outcomes.
Strong executive judgment with the ability to prioritize competing demands and balance innovation, risk, cost, organizational capacity and readiness.
Proven people leader who builds organizational capability, develops senior leaders and creates clarity and accountability.
Exceptional relationship builder and influencer who can navigate a decentralized, relationship-driven organization while advancing enterprise priorities.
Clear and compelling communicator who translates complex technology issues into understandable organizational implications and decisions for technical and non-technical audiences.
Proven people leader who builds organizational capability, develops senior leaders and creates clarity and accountability.
Strong business, financial and commercial acumen, including technology investment, vendor management and benefits realization.
Data-driven and digitally fluent executive who can establish trusted information, enable analytics and guide responsible AI and automation adoption with appropriate governance and human oversight.
Values-based leader who demonstrates integrity, humility, stewardship and a strong service orientation.
Comfortable with complexity and ambiguity, with the ability to bring clarity, structure and direction to challenging organizational situations.

Compensation

The target hiring range for this position is $244,046.40 to $305,052.80 with a maximum of $366,059.20.

Placement in the salary range will be based on factors such as market conditions, internal equity, and candidate experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the role.

The Salvation Army will provide reasonable accommodation upon request. Please email Recruitment.Accommodations@salvationarmy.ca

jobs.description:
Please note that we will never request payment or bank account information at any stage of the recruitment process. As we continue to grow our teams, we urge you to be cautious of fraudulent job postings or recruitment activities that misuse our company name and information. Please protect your personal information during any recruitment process. While Monks may contact potential candidates via LinkedIn, all applications must be submitted through our official website (monks.com/careers).

About The Role

As an Associate Director, Analytics, you will lead complex analytics and data science engagements, bringing together strong quantitative expertise, strategic thinking, and client leadership.

This role requires a strong foundation in data science and advanced analytics
. You should be comfortable working with sophisticated analytical methodologies, evaluating data science approaches and outputs, and translating complex quantitative findings into clear business recommendations.

At the Associate Director level, you will also lead teams and workstreams, influence senior stakeholders, and help shape the analytical approach to complex client challenges. You may not be coding or building models every day, but you should have sufficient data science depth to credibly guide the work and challenge the methodology.

Responsibilities

Data Science & Advanced Analytics

Lead advanced analytics and data science work across complex client engagements. Apply and guide approaches such as statistical modeling, predictive analytics, experimentation, segmentation, forecasting, machine learning, or other advanced quantitative methodologies as appropriate to the business problem.

Evaluate analytical approaches and outputs, identify limitations and opportunities, and ensure that methodologies are rigorous, actionable, and connected to client objectives.

Complex Program & Engagement Leadership

Lead complex analytics projects or programs end to end across one or more accounts—shaping the analytical approach, orchestrating cross-functional teams, and owning outcomes at a senior level.

Strategic Analytics & Client Advisory

Translate sophisticated analysis and data science outputs into clear business implications and recommendations. Connect analytical findings to the client's broader marketing and business agenda.

Serve as a senior analytics partner to clients and internal stakeholders, helping frame ambiguous business questions into analytical problems that can be solved with data.

Team & Technical Leadership

Lead and develop analytics and data science talent, set expectations for analytical quality, and provide guidance on methodologies and approaches across multiple workstreams.

Partner effectively with data scientists, analysts, media teams, strategists, engineers, and other specialists to deliver integrated solutions.

Early Account Economics

Take first-line accountability for the economics of your workstreams—including utilization, scope discipline, and margin within your remit—and partner with account leadership on planning and resourcing.

Client Advisory & Growth

Build credible senior client relationships and identify opportunities where analytics, data science, measurement, or AI capabilities can address additional client needs.

AI-Enabled Delivery & Innovation

Identify qualified AI use cases and opportunities to incorporate AI-enabled approaches into analytics and measurement. Help evaluate where emerging technologies can create measurable value rather than applying AI for its own sake.

About You

The Essentials

7+ years of experience in analytics, data science, quantitative consulting, measurement, or a related field across an agency, consultancy, holding company, technology company, or sophisticated in-house environment
Demonstrated data science experience is required, with a strong understanding of advanced quantitative methodologies such as statistical modeling, predictive analytics, experimentation, machine learning, forecasting, segmentation, or related approaches
Experience leading complex analytics or data science projects from business problem definition through analysis, interpretation, and recommendation
Ability to evaluate and guide sophisticated analytical work, including methodology, assumptions, limitations, and business implications
Ability to translate complex quantitative findings into clear, actionable recommendations for non-technical and senior audiences
Experience partnering with or leading data scientists, analysts, and other technical specialists
Experience leading and developing teams
Demonstrated influence across functions, client teams, or portfolios
Credible senior client relationships and the ability to advise, not just deliver
Emerging account-economics literacy, including utilization, scope, and margin within a remit

Strong Plus

Hands-on experience with programming and analytical tools such as SQL, Python, R, or similar
Experience with experimentation, causal inference, marketing measurement, incrementality, attribution, or other advanced measurement approaches
Experience applying machine learning or predictive modeling to marketing or business problems
Experience integrating GenAI or agentic platforms with measurable outcomes
Quantified contribution to account growth or scope expansion
Recognized domain authority through frameworks, methodologies, or thought leadership
Experience developing reusable analytical methodologies, tools, or accelerators
Senior platform partnership experience with Google, Meta, Adobe, Amazon, or similar
Cross-domain experience across more than one IMA practice area

jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What you'll be doing

Our AI team builds enterprise capabilities that support a wide range of users across the organization, from end users to technology teams and low-code or no-code builders. As a Principal Product Scaler – AI Engineering, you'll build the engineering foundation that helps us repeatedly deliver high-quality AI products safely, efficiently, and at scale. You'll architect and develop the reusable components, software development kits, testing frameworks, and delivery patterns that move us from individual implementations to a mature product engineering model. You'll establish the standards for how AI products are designed, built, tested, packaged, released, and monitored in production. Working closely with data scientists, engineers, and technology partners, you'll help turn strong prototypes into reliable enterprise products while strengthening the team's overall engineering capability.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview.

How you'll succeed

Build scalable engineering foundations
- Design and develop software development kits, libraries, reusable components, templates, and reference implementations that accelerate delivery across the AI portfolio and reduce repeated effort across teams.
Establish engineering excellence -
Define and implement standards for code structure, testing, code review, versioning, packaging, documentation, release management, and production readiness for AI and Generative AI products.
Advance AI quality and reliability
- Create automated testing, evaluation, regression, monitoring, and observability patterns that support both traditional software quality and the unique behavior of probabilistic AI systems.
Drive efficient delivery
- Establish continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) patterns, quality gates, and repeatable workflows that help teams move from experiment to production with greater speed and consistency.
Enable adoption across teams -
Design interfaces and developer experiences that make enterprise AI capabilities easy to consume for technology teams, other AI teams, and low-code or no-code solution builders.
Elevate team capability
- Review architecture and code for critical products, coach AI practitioners on engineering best practices, and help the team adopt effective agentic development workflows, tooling, and guardrails.

Who you are

You are a hands-on senior engineering leader
. You have experience operating at a Staff, Principal, Lead Engineer, or equivalent level, and you enjoy both designing systems and writing production-quality code.
You can demonstrate experience in
system design, application programming interface (API) and software development kit (SDK) design, testing, CI/CD, versioning, observability, and production operations. It’s an asset if you have built platforms, frameworks, developer tooling, or reusable services used by multiple teams.
You give meaning to data
. You understand the engineering challenges of taking AI and Generative AI solutions from experimentation into production, and you know that quality for AI systems requires more than traditional unit testing.
You look beyond the moment.
You're excited by the opportunity to shape how agentic software development evolves, including workflows, repository design, testing approaches, review practices, context management, and governance for increasingly autonomous delivery.
You're motivated by collective success
. You influence engineers, data scientists, technology partners, and leaders through strong partnership, sound judgment, and a commitment to raising the capability of the broader organization.
You act like an owner
. You naturally identify repeated patterns, remove friction from the development lifecycle, and build practical solutions that help teams deliver faster, more safely, and with greater consistency.
Values matter to you
. You bring your real self to work, and you live our values - trust, teamwork, and accountability.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

Join the Renewed Seneca, The Next Seneca.

At Seneca Polytechnic, we offer a flexible working environment that supports innovative thinking and encourages exploring new ideas and approaches. As we adapt to an ever-changing landscape, we continue to promote opportunities for career growth and development. We focus on health and well-being in all ways to provide great employee experience.

Chief Information Officer

Do you believe that technology, data, and digital platforms should open new possibilities? Are you motivated by the opportunity to lead large scale digital transformation while advancing equity, innovation, and employee and student success at one of Canada’s leading post-secondary institutions?

Seneca Polytechnic is seeking a Chief Information Officer
to provide institution-wide leadership and strategic direction for information technology, digital platforms, enterprise systems, and data. Reporting to the Vice President, Students and IT, you will play a critical role in shaping Seneca’s digital future, ensuring secure, reliable, and innovative technology services that support teaching, learning, research, and operations.

In this critical role, you will lead IT modernization, strengthen Seneca’s leadership in artificial intelligence, and partner with academic and administrative leaders to ensure technology investments deliver meaningful organizational value.

How You Approach the Role

Seneca operates in a complex post-secondary environment with rapid technological change, evolving learner needs, and increasing cybersecurity risks. In this context, you will

Set a clear and compelling vision for Seneca’s information technology and digital strategy, aligned with institutional priorities and long-term plans.
Lead the development and execution of a multi-year IT and digital transformation roadmap, including enterprise architecture and technology governance.
Advance innovation by collaboratively identifying and leveraging emerging technologies that enhance teaching, learning, research, and institutional effectiveness.
Maintain and grow Seneca’s leadership in artificial intelligence, ensuring responsible, ethical, and impactful application across the institution.
Embed principles of equity, diversity, and inclusion into technology strategies, policies, and service delivery.
Build strong partnerships with academic and administrative leaders to translate institutional needs into effective technology solutions.
Foster trust through transparent decision-making, thoughtful communication, and consistent follow through.

What You’ll Do in This Role

As CIO, you will provide strategic, operational, and people leadership across a broad and integrated portfolio, leading a senior IT leadership team and fostering collaboration, accountability, and high performance. You will ensure the secure, reliable, and effective delivery of enterprise technology services while overseeing cybersecurity, data privacy, system resilience, business continuity, and compliance. You will guide the modernization and lifecycle management of enterprise platforms, establish meaningful performance measures, and lead budgeting, resource allocation, vendor management, and contract negotiations. You will also strengthen staff engagement, professional development, and workforce sustainability within a complex and evolving technology environment.

What You Bring

You are a seasoned technology leader who balances strategic vision with operational excellence and brings extensive, progressive experience leading complex IT organizations, enterprise systems, digital transformation, and multi-year initiatives. You exercise strong judgment in managing risk, security, and compliance while enabling innovation, agility, and evidence-based decision-making through data, analytics, and emerging tools. An effective communicator and collaborative partner, you translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable insights and influence diverse stakeholder groups. You have built inclusive, high-performing leadership teams and lead with integrity, accountability, transparency, and respect.

Seneca supports flexible and inclusive work practices, recognizing diverse leadership styles and experiences. We recognize that leadership experience may be gained through a variety of career paths, including community-based work, sector transitions, or lived experience alongside formal roles. A combination of education and experience will be considered.

About Teneo

Teneo is the global CEO advisory firm. We partner with our clients globally to do great things for a better future.

Drawing upon our global team and expansive network of senior advisors, we provide advisory services across our five business segments on a stand-alone or fully integrated basis to help our clients solve complex business challenges. Our clients include a significant number of the Fortune 100 and FTSE 100, as well as other cor­po­ra­tions, financial insti­tu­tions and organizations.

Our full range of advisory services includes strategic com­mu­ni­ca­tions, investor relations, financial trans­ac­tions and restruc­tur­ing, management consulting, physical and cyber risk, orga­ni­za­tion­al design, board and executive search, geopolitics and government affairs, corporate governance, ESG and DE&I.

The firm has more than 1,800 employees located in 50+ offices around the world.

Description

Teneo Digital advises the world's leading CEOs and organizations on how to show up, compete and win in a digital-first world, where reputation is shaped across social media, search, paid campaigns, AI-generated answers and emerging platforms.

We work at the intersection of strategy, communications and digital, helping clients navigate how influence is evolving and translating those changes into practical communications, campaign and reputation strategies.

We're looking for a senior digital strategist to help build Teneo Canada's capability at the intersection of digital strategy, campaigns, AI and reputation. This is a client-facing advisory role, working with senior communications and corporate affairs leaders to develop digital strategies, lead campaign strategy and oversee execution with specialist partners and translate emerging trends into practical recommendations that drive business outcomes.

Day to day, you'll help clients understand where digital influence is moving, how technology is reshaping communications, and how to apply those insights to campaigns, reputation management and executive positioning.

This person does not need to be a media buyer or AI engineer but should understand those disciplines well enough to lead strategy, manage specialist partners and confidently advise clients.

Responsibilities

Advise clients on digital strategy across reputation, stakeholder engagement, social, search, paid media, AI-driven discovery and executive visibility, connecting digital considerations to broader business and communications objectives.
Develop digital and integrated communications strategies, helping define audiences, narratives, channels, objectives and measurement frameworks while coordinating with specialist internal and external partners.
Lead and contribute to client workstreams, workshops and strategic discussions, translating complex digital and emerging-technology trends into practical recommendations for senior communications and corporate affairs leaders.
Contribute to multidisciplinary teams working on complex or high-stakes client situations, including assignments where digital is only one part of the broader strategic challenge.
Develop client-ready deliverables including presentations, strategic recommendations, campaign plans and points of view requiring minimal oversight.
Guide digital reputation and intelligence initiatives across social listening, search, GEO, AI visibility and emerging platforms, identifying risks, stakeholder dynamics and opportunities for clients.
Work with paid media, creative and analytics partners to ensure campaigns and digital programs are strategically sound, measurable and aligned with client objectives, without necessarily acting as the hands-on platform operator.
Help build Teneo’s digital advisory offerings, including new methodologies, playbooks and points of view across digital reputation, emerging platforms and AI.
Mentor junior team members, providing direction on research, analysis, reporting and client deliverables while helping build capability across the team.
Stay at the forefront of developments across digital platforms, social, search, AI, LLMs and emerging technologies, proactively bringing new ideas and implications to clients and colleagues.

Qualifications

6+ years’ experience in digital strategy, strategic communications, corporate affairs, reputation management, management consulting or related advisory work.
Experience supporting or advising senior stakeholders on digital strategy, reputation, stakeholder engagement, transformation or other complex business issues.
Demonstrated ability to structure complex problems, develop strategic recommendations and coordinate multidisciplinary teams through execution.
Strong understanding of integrated communications and campaigns spanning owned, earned, shared and paid channels, with experience developing strategy rather than simply executing tactics.
Ability to quickly understand unfamiliar business, reputation and stakeholder issues and identify where digital insight or strategy can add value.
Working knowledge of paid media and ad-buying ecosystems, with the ability to collaborate effectively with specialist agencies and vendors, challenge recommendations and oversee execution.
Strong understanding of digital platforms, search, GEO, AI-driven discovery, social listening and how digital reputation and information environments are evolving.
Experience using digital analytics, research or social listening to identify trends, assess stakeholder dynamics, measure performance and translate findings into strategic recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop clear, executive-ready presentations, recommendations and points of view.
Experience managing client workstreams and mentoring junior team members in a fast-paced, client-driven environment.
Curious, strategically minded and comfortable working in ambiguity, with a demonstrated ability to translate emerging technologies and digital trends into practical client opportunities.

The Director of FP&A, R&D acts as the strategic finance partner to Engineering, Product, and Data/ML leadership, owning the R&D operating plan and establishing LLM economics as a fundamental financial discipline. This role manages the P&L for R&D headcount and Cost of Revenue (CoR) for AI in production, driving efficiency through direct engagement with our data stack (BigQuery/dbt).

What You'll Do

Partner day to day with engineering, product, and data leaders as their trusted finance counterpart.
Build the analyses that shape build-vs-buy, pricing, and infrastructure decisions.
Support foundation-model and cloud vendor negotiations with data-backed positions.
Deliver clear, concise reporting and variance commentary to the CFO, FP&A leadership, and the board.
Own the R&D budget, forecast, and headcount plan across Engineering, Product, and Data/ML. Drive the re-forecast cycle and keep hiring plans tied to output and priorities.
Make LLM/inference and cloud compute cost a first-class, closely monitored metric. Build the model that tracks unit costs; monitor spend daily; and partner with engineering to find and defend efficiency. This is not a monthly-close afterthought, it's a core operating metric of the business.
Own the connection between usage, inference cost, and gross margin. Model the margin impact of new products, pricing changes, and model/infrastructure choices, and make the tradeoffs legible to leadership.
Bring financial rigor to major R&D spend decisions including foundation-model and API contracts, cloud commitments, data, and dev tooling, including negotiation support and ROI cases.

8+ years in FP&A / corporate finance, with meaningful time supporting R&D, Engineering, or a technical/product org.
Deep comfort with SaaS and AI/usage-based economics: CoR, gross margin, unit economics, and how infrastructure/inference cost drives them.
Strong SQL (BigQuery a major plus) and expert Excel/Sheets modeling, with clean, maintainable model architecture.
Strong grasp of how R&D spend flows through the P&L.
Ability to be a genuine partner to technical leaders, holding substantive conversations with engineering or ML leads to translate technical work into financial views.
Precise, low-ego, self-directed, and concise work ethic.
Nice to have: Experience at a high-growth AI/ML company, familiarity with modern data stacks, contract negotiation experience, people management experience, and CPA/CA/CFA.
Nice to have: Familiarity with a modern data stack (dbt, EPMs) and building repeatable, auditable finance pipelines.
